searchText: In my opinion, frames should be treated as first-class transactions and have their own gas limits, rather than sharing a single EIP-7825 limit for all of them. a primary goal of 7825 is to limit dos attacks. since a transaction is fully settled upon completion, there are many less knobs to turn to pull of a dos and you will likely need to pay dearly. frames are not fully settled upon completion and future frames can cancel out storage usage (0 -> 1 -> 0 pattern) so it very much increases the surface area for dos. i think the only way we could support full 7825 limits per frame is to settle each frame after completion fully. but that remove the ability to handle batches nicely. so i think we should keep 7825 per-tx I don't see any conflict here EIP-8037 separated state gas into a distinct gas dimension; this dimension does not affect execution capacity—since state changes have long-term implications—and state gas is constrained solely by block size, regardless of the transaction mix. I believe that frame completeness and atomicity can certainly be reconciled in this context. I recall a proposal to group atomic transactions together to enforce their collective completion; frames are essentially just another approach to this—they are clearly delineated to allow for static analysis as a complete transaction, so the execution behavior is effectively the same. explicit 2d gas merged: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12062 i think we want to target this for devnet-0?

a primary goal of 7825 is to limit dos attacks. since a transaction is fully settled upon completion, there are many less knobs to turn to pull of a dos and you will likely need to pay dearly.

frames are not fully settled upon completion and future frames can cancel out storage usage (0 -> 1 -> 0 pattern) so it very much increases the surface area for dos. i think the only way we could support full 7825 limits per frame is to settle each frame after completion fully. but that remove the ability to handle batches nicely. so i think we should keep 7825 per-tx

excerpts.author: gaxanh
excerpts.content:
I don't see any conflict here

EIP-8037 separated state gas into a distinct gas dimension; this dimension does not affect execution capacity—since state changes have long-term implications—and state gas is constrained solely by block size, regardless of the transaction mix.

I believe that frame completeness and atomicity can certainly be reconciled in this context. I recall a proposal to group atomic transactions together to enforce their collective completion; frames are essentially just another approach to this—they are clearly delineated to allow for static analysis as a complete transaction, so the execution behavior is effectively the same.
